title: Knee Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset severe monoarticular knee pain, erythema, warmth, and swelling. Pain began suddenly overnight — classic podagra (great toe) or knee involvement. History reveals dietary triggers (red meat, seafood, alcohol) or diuretic use. Gout is caused by monosodium urate crystal deposition in joints from chronic hyperuricemia. Definitive diagnosis: joint aspiration with synovial fluid analysis under polarized light microscopy — needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals. Do NOT give NSAIDs in renal impairment. First-line acute treatment: NSAIDs (indomethacin or naproxen), colchicine (within 36h of onset), or corticosteroids (oral prednisone or intra-articular injection). Colchicine: avoid in renal/hepatic impairment, CYP3A4 interactions. Long-term urate-lowering: allopurinol or febuxostat (start after acute flare resolves, with colchicine prophylaxis for 3-6 months). Target uric acid <6.0 mg/dL (or <5.0 for tophaceous gout).
chief_complaint: Acute severe knee pain, redness, swelling

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular
stacks.finding: Screen for endocarditis if septic joint suspected.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Extremities / Knee
stacks.finding: Monoarticular: hot, swollen, erythematous knee. Exquisite tenderness. Limited ROM.

stacks.label: Arthrocentesis + synovial fluid analysis
stacks.finding: Negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals under polarized light. WBC 2000-50,000. Rule out septic arthritis. Gram stain and culture.

stacks.label: BMP / Uric acid
stacks.finding: Uric acid may be normal during acute flare. Assess renal function (affects NSAID/colchicine use).

stacks.label: NSAIDs (Indomethacin / Naproxen) or Colchicine
stacks.finding: First-line within 36h. Colchicine: avoid in renal/hepatic impairment. Alternatives: prednisone or intra-articular steroids.

stacks.label: Allopurinol (after acute flare)
stacks.finding: Start after flare resolves + colchicine prophylaxis. Target uric acid <6.0.

physical_exam.musculoskeletal: Monoarticular: knee hot, swollen, erythematous, exquisitely tender.
